_readme: This is log.json, exported by VIGIL, an Android app that executes a weekly plan (plan.json) written by a planner AI, and records what happened. The app never plans, judges or decides anything; all intelligence lives in the plan. HOW THE APP BEHAVES. Each directive has a trigger: a time of day in the phone's local time ("time"), the user's adhan app posting its prayer notification ("adhan"; the app does not compute prayer times), or listed apps being opened too often or used too long in one go ("app_usage"). When it triggers, the phone shows a full-screen takeover with the directive's checklist. Steps appear one at a time, and each can only be ticked once its min_seconds have passed. The takeover closes when every step is ticked (directive_completed), when the user holds the dismiss button for about 10 seconds (directive_dismissed), or by itself after 90 minutes as the active takeover (directive_timed_out). One takeover shows at a time; others wait their turn, and a directive that is already showing or waiting is not opened twice (the repeat is logged as repeated). A time trigger the phone could not act on within 30 minutes of its moment (phone off or asleep) is logged as missed instead of being shown late. Quiet mode is a manual switch. While it is on, each directive follows its "quiet" field: queue = held (queued_quiet) and fired once when quiet mode ends, with trigger "quiet_queue"; silent = shown without sound or vibration ("silent": true); ignore = not shown (skipped_quiet); override = tier 3 only, rings anyway if settings.allow_quiet_override is "true", otherwise shown silently. Switching quiet mode on also applies to takeovers that already fired: the one on screen goes silent, and waiting ones follow their rule (a held or skipped one closes as dropped, and a held one is logged queued_quiet too). "I'm not okay today" mode is switched on by the user and lasts until the next day boundary (the plan's day_boundary, 04:00 by default). Meanwhile only the directives in bad_day.keep fire: the others are logged as skipped_bad_day, and a takeover showing or waiting when it was switched on closes as bypassed_bad_day. These are NOT failures; the user was honest about a hard day. Read them with compassion, never as weakness. When the plan's expires time passes, the app logs plan_expired and runs the plan's fallback_plan, or, if there is none, a built-in minimal plan (prayers, water, sleep; its directive ids start with "default-"). On a bad day the fallback_plan keeps all its directives; the built-in plan keeps only its own essentials (prayers and sleep). HOW TO READ THIS FILE. "events" lists what happened in time order, starting at "since" (null = the whole log). ts is the phone's local time with its UTC offset ("timezone" names the zone). Fields that do not apply to an event are left out. takeover_id groups one takeover's events: directive_fired, its step_completed events, then the event that closed it. step_index counts from 0. duration_s is in seconds: for step_completed, since that step appeared; for the closing event, since the directive fired, including any time it waited behind another takeover. scheduled_for is the planned moment of a time trigger; ts can be later. tier is 1 (nudge), 2 (short checklist) or 3 (full sequence). Triggers "debug" and "adhan_test" and directive "vigil-demo" are the user testing the app: they are left out of "summary"; ignore them. "summary" counts outcomes per directive id and gives avg_completion_s; it counts, it does not judge. "event_types" explains every event type. "plan" identifies the last imported plan. "settings" lists app settings that change behaviour. Use this log together with vision.md and the last plan.json to write next week's plan.json (see HANDOFF.md in the VIGIL repository). Treat every outcome as information for a better plan, not as grounds for blame.

event_types.plan_imported: A plan was imported and became active (detail: week_of and generated_by).
event_types.plan_import_failed: An import was rejected; the previous plan stayed active (detail: the first error).
event_types.plan_expired: The plan's expires time passed; the app now runs its fallback_plan or, without one, the built-in minimal plan (detail says which).
event_types.directive_fired: A trigger happened and a takeover opened (trigger, scheduled_for, silent, steps_total). If another takeover was on screen, this one waited for it to close.
event_types.step_completed: A checklist step was ticked (step_index from 0, step_text, duration_s since the step appeared).
event_types.directive_completed: Every step was ticked (duration_s since it fired).
event_types.directive_dismissed: Closed early by holding the dismiss button for about 10 seconds (steps_done of steps_total, duration_s since it fired).
event_types.directive_timed_out: Still open 90 minutes after it fired, so it closed itself (steps_done of steps_total).
event_types.bypassed_bad_day: Closed while showing or waiting because the user switched on "I'm not okay today" and it is not in bad_day.keep. Not a failure.
event_types.skipped_bad_day: Not shown because "I'm not okay today" was on and it is not in bad_day.keep. Not a failure.
event_types.queued_quiet: Triggered during quiet mode (quiet: queue): held, and fired when quiet mode ends.
event_types.skipped_quiet: Not shown because quiet mode was on (quiet: ignore).
event_types.missed: A time trigger's moment passed more than 30 minutes before the app could act (phone off or asleep), so it was not shown late (scheduled_for is the planned moment).
event_types.dropped: A takeover (showing or waiting) closed without a result, with the reason in detail: its directive is no longer in the running plan (after a new import or the switch to the fallback plan), quiet mode was switched on while it waited (quiet: queue or ignore), or the developer kill switch was used.
event_types.repeated: The directive fired again while it was already showing or waiting, so it was not opened a second time.
event_types.quiet_off: Quiet mode switched off; directives held by it fire now.
event_types.bad_day_on: "I'm not okay today" switched on; it lasts until the day boundary (detail).
event_types.bad_day_off: "I'm not okay today" ended (detail: switched off by the user, or the day ended).
